title: Fynaptix · Defense Tech Research
heading: Defense Technology Intelligence
subheading: AI battlefield software, drones, autonomy & European rearmament
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Defense names carry policy, program-concentration, and valuation risk. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: NATO's latest tally shows European Allies and Canada raised 2025 defence spending by over $90B in 2021 prices (~$139B nominal) — nearly 20% YoY; five Allies are already on track to hit the 3.5%-of-GDP core guideline in 2026 and 17 to hit the 1.5% broader-security guideline, both years ahead of the 2035 deadline set at the Hague summit, while the EU's €800B 'ReArm Europe' framework keeps the multi-year runway intact

kpis.sub: 2026 YTD · DEFENSE TECH VC, ALREADY WELL PAST 2025's $9.6B FULL-YEAR RECORD
kpis.label: Early-stage defense-tech rounds are now pricing at 17x-50x revenue, and the Bank for International Settlements has begun likening the sector's forward-looking, scarcity-driven valuations to the AI-infrastructure buildout it already calls bubble-like; Anduril's targeted raise (last discussed near $100B, with prediction markets now floating $112.5B by Sep 30) remains unclosed roughly nine weeks after first being reported on Jul 24

Defense Autonomous Warfare Group request inside a record $75B FY27 drone/counter-drone budget ask; separately, 98% of Golden Dome's requested $17.5B needs a reconciliation bill rather than the base budget, so a continuing resolution wouldn't just freeze the program at FY26 levels — it would leave it with no funding at all, since Golden Dome has no prior-year baseline to revert to, a risk Gen. Guetlein flagged Aug 12 and September reporting says has only hardened

kpis.sub: AVAV ARMY LOCUST X3 LASER AWARD · SEP 2-3
kpis.label: The Pentagon's first-ever production contract for a directed-energy system, funding dozens of 30kW LOCUST X3 laser units under the Enduring-High Energy Laser program for layered counter-drone defense; lands on top of the Sep 9 Q1 FY27 beat ($480.5M revenue, $1.5B funded backlog, +37% YoY) — shares rose as much as 6% on the laser news alone

tiers.label: Established / Software & Primes
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: Shares near $177-178 (Sep 20, ~$427B market cap) after UBS's Karl Keirstead lifted his target to $250 from $220 on Sep 15 — the third upward revision this year — calling Palantir the cheapest AI software name on customer-demand-outpacing-capacity grounds following AIPCon 11; the stock has added roughly 6% since last week's ~$167 print, still trading well north of 100x trailing earnings
rows.watch for: CEO Alex Karp told CNBC on Sep 17 that leading AI labs may need to be nationalized to cap liability — a new regulatory-risk thread — and Michael Burry's unretracted case that the market cap could eventually fall below $100B still hasn't been addressed by the company

rows.angle: Shares recovered to roughly €1,012-1,028 (Sep 16-18) from last week's ~€988 low, helped by Deutsche Bank's Sep 1 Buy reiteration and a new $7.3M US Marine Corps unmanned-ground-vehicle order, but remain down roughly 34-36% YTD and still underperforming the DAX since June's F126 frigate-program cancellation
rows.watch for: JPMorgan kept Rheinmetall at Hold on Sep 10 even as 18 of 18 covering analysts hold Buy/Strong-Buy ratings and the average target (~€1,641) implies ~60% upside — the gap between the cautious desk and the bullish consensus is still unresolved

rows.angle: New CEO Sam Mehta and new board chair Lewis Hay are settling in after Chris Kubasik's Aug 17 conduct-related ouster; L3Harris landed a $4.7B Lockheed Martin deal and its VAMPIRE/APKWS systems saw further operational use by Ukrainian forces, but shares remain down 16% over the past month and about 35% off their all-time high
rows.watch for: The company still hasn't detailed what triggered Kubasik's removal, and Golden Dome's FY27 funding is now described as being at real risk since 98% of its request needs a reconciliation bill a stopgap can't provide

rows.angle: Shares climbed to roughly 2,024-2,043p (Sep 16-19), an ~11% recovery off the Sep 14 low, as confidence reasserted itself in the record £84.0B H1 order backlog and July's raised full-year guidance (8-10% sales growth, 11-13% EPS growth)
rows.watch for: The rally still leaves shares below the 2,360p 52-week high, and H2 execution against the raised guidance remains unproven

tiers.label: High-Growth Autonomy Pure-Plays
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: The Army awarded AeroVironment $464.8M for LOCUST X3 high-energy laser systems (Sep 2-3) — the Pentagon's first-ever production contract for a directed-energy system — on top of the Sep 9 Q1 FY27 beat ($480.5M revenue, $1.5B backlog, +37% YoY); shares rose as much as 6% on the laser news alone
rows.watch for: The securities-fraud class actions tied to the SCAR/BADGER restatement are still working through the courts, and shares remain roughly 36% below where they started the year despite the recent run

rows.angle: Sell-side targets kept climbing after the Q2 beat-and-raise (Canaccord $135, BTIG $104, Clear Street $86; consensus $105.62 across 21 analysts, Strong Buy), and GE Aerospace's GEK800 engine testing keeps CCA-engine optionality alive toward a targeted $150M of 2027 turbojet revenue
rows.watch for: Kratos qualified for both Gauntlet 1 and Gauntlet 2 of the Pentagon's Drone Dominance Program but again failed to make the Sep 18 leaderboard — a real data point against the autonomy-optionality part of the thesis, even with the stock still down 37% YTD

rows.angle: Teal Drones (Red Cat's subsidiary) competed in Gauntlet II's Close Quarters Battle category but didn't place in the top five (Sep 18-19) — Neros, ORQA, XTEND, Vector and ModalAI took the top spots instead — while shares barely moved, underperforming even the muted broader drone-sector reaction
rows.watch for: This is the second straight negative data point after August's insider share sales; the Blue Ops/Havoc maritime-autonomy story and the Apium Swarm Robotics integration still need to show up in contracted revenue rather than platform narrative

rows.angle: Ascent Aerosystems (Ondas's subsidiary) missed the top five in Gauntlet II's Deep Strike category (Sep 18), while the core Sentrycs/Iron Drone counter-UAS business and a Mistral-unit loitering-munitions program with the Army continue in the background; shares remain down roughly 22% YTD
rows.watch for: The Q2 EPS miss (-$0.19 vs -$0.13 expected) and the Form 144 insider-sale filing are still live concerns, and the Gauntlet II result adds a competitive-positioning question on top of the balance-sheet one

private_watchlist.name: Anduril
private_watchlist.note: Talks first reported Jul 24 remain unclosed roughly nine weeks later, as of Sep 21 — prediction markets are now pricing whether the eventual mark could reach $112.5B by Sep 30. On Sep 15 Anduril unveiled armed FQ-44 Fury configurations (JDAMs, Small Diameter Bombs, low-cost cruise missiles), and a Boeing-Anduril interceptor advanced in the Army's IFPC Second Interceptor competition on Sep 9 — real revenue-scaling news even as the funding round itself drags on.

private_watchlist.name: Shield AI
private_watchlist.note: No new financing this period; still marked by the ~$1.5-2B round (Mar 2026) that valued the company at $12.7B. Continuing to compete for the Navy's up-to-$800M ISR task-order pool using the V-BAT drone; Greece's parliament approved a €71M program in June for ten additional V-BAT systems (20 aircraft), part of a broader run of NATO eastern-flank interest that includes Poland's earlier award.

private_watchlist.name: Saronic
private_watchlist.note: No new financing this period; still marked by the $1.75B Series D (Kleiner Perkins) plus early-September's $55M add-on that set the ~$9.25B mark. Continuing to build out the Port of Gulfport autonomous-ship test site toward a stated target of 20+ autonomous surface vessels a year by 2027 out of its Franklin, Louisiana shipyard.

private_watchlist.name: Helsing
private_watchlist.note: No new financing this period; still marked by the $1.8B Series E closed Jul 13, 2026 (Lightspeed, General Catalyst, JPMorgan, Iconiq) — the largest defence-tech round in European history. Continues fielding the HX-2 strike drone in Ukraine and building out its Altra battle-management software and CA-1 Europa uncrewed-fighter concept.

bear_case.title: Public-market valuations still stretched, even after this week's rally
bear_case.description: Palantir's climb to ~$177-178 on UBS's fresh $250 target keeps the stock well above 100x trailing earnings, and Michael Burry's unretracted case that the market cap could eventually fall below $100B hasn't gone away; the S&P Aerospace & Defense sub-index trades around 32x forward earnings versus roughly 20x for the broader S&P 500 — a premium the sector has to keep earning, not just borrowing against sentiment.

bear_case.title: Private-market valuations are drawing bubble comparisons of their own
bear_case.description: Early-stage defense-tech rounds are now pricing at 17x-50x revenue, and Anduril's targeted valuation — last discussed near $100B, with prediction markets now floating $112.5B by Sep 30 — remains unclosed roughly nine weeks after first being reported; the Bank for International Settlements has begun comparing the sector's forward-looking, scarcity-driven pricing to the AI-infrastructure buildout it has already flagged as bubble-like.

bear_case.title: The Pentagon's own drone competitions are favoring private newcomers over listed pure-plays
bear_case.description: Sep 18's Gauntlet II results put Neros, Perennial Autonomy, ORQA, XTEND and ModalAI atop the leaderboard, while Red Cat's Teal Drones, Ondas's Ascent Aerosystems and Kratos — all three publicly listed — missed the top five in their categories; a program built explicitly to surface the best autonomy vendors isn't currently surfacing the ones investors can buy on a US exchange.

bear_case.title: Golden Dome's funding structure means a stopgap doesn't freeze it — it zeroes it
bear_case.description: 98% of Golden Dome's requested $17.5B FY27 funding needs a reconciliation bill, not the base defense budget, and a continuing resolution locks agencies at prior-year spending — which for Golden Dome is nothing, since the program has no FY26 baseline to revert to; Gen. Guetlein's Aug 12 warning has only hardened as September reporting describes the program's near-term progress as being at real risk.

bear_case.title: Leadership and governance disruption at the primes hasn't fully resolved
bear_case.description: L3Harris now has both a new CEO (Sam Mehta) and a new board chair (Lewis Hay) following Chris Kubasik's conduct-related ouster, and the stock remains 35% off its all-time high even as new contract wins (the $4.7B Lockheed Martin deal, VAMPIRE/APKWS combat use in Ukraine) suggest the underlying business is intact; the market hasn't yet decided whether this is a clean transition or an unfinished story.

bear_case.title: AeroVironment's legal overhang survives even a run of good news
bear_case.description: The $464.8M Army laser contract and the Sep 9 earnings beat have driven a real recovery, but the securities-fraud class actions tied to the SCAR/BADGER restatement are still working through the courts; neither a laser contract nor a strong quarter retroactively resolves the disclosure issue that triggered the litigation.

catalysts.title: BAE Systems shares extend recovery to ~2,043p
catalysts.description: An ~11% climb off the Sep 14 low as investor confidence reasserts itself in the record £84.0B H1 order backlog and July's raised guidance.

catalysts.title: Pentagon names Gauntlet II Drone Dominance winners; listed pure-plays miss the podium
catalysts.description: Neros topped Close Quarters Battle (88.1) and Perennial Autonomy topped Deep Strike (80.1); Red Cat's Teal Drones and Ondas's Ascent Aerosystems both missed the top five, and Kratos again failed to place.

catalysts.title: Palantir CEO Alex Karp tells CNBC AI labs may need to be nationalized to cap liability
catalysts.description: Adds a new regulatory-risk thread alongside UBS's Sep 15 target hike to $250 — a reminder that policy risk can move PLTR as fast as earnings do.

catalysts.title: UBS lifts Palantir target to $250 from $220, its third raise this year
catalysts.description: Analyst Karl Keirstead cites customer demand outpacing capacity after AIPCon 11; shares near $177-178, up from ~$167 a week earlier.

catalysts.title: Anduril unveils armed FQ-44 Fury configurations
catalysts.description: JDAMs, Small Diameter Bombs and low-cost cruise missiles integrated onto the CCA airframe, expanding its combat role even as the reported $100B funding round remains unclosed roughly nine weeks after first being reported.

catalysts.title: AeroVironment wins $464.8M Army contract for LOCUST X3 laser systems
catalysts.description: The Pentagon's first-ever production contract for a directed-energy system; shares rose as much as 6% on the news, on top of the Sep 9 earnings beat.

etfs.name: Global X Defense Tech
etfs.summary: Tilted toward Palantir and autonomy pure-plays, with almost 38% annualized returns since its Sept 2023 inception; this week's PLTR rally to ~$177-178 and BAE's climb toward 2,043p give the fund a stronger tailwind than the Gauntlet II results gave its smaller drone-pure-play holdings

etfs.name: iShares US Aerospace & Defense
etfs.summary: Largest in category at ~$13.3B AUM and 0.38% expense ratio; broad US primes exposure (RTX, Boeing, Lockheed alongside LHX and AVAV) has stayed largely insulated from this week's small-cap Gauntlet II fallout

etfs.name: Invesco Aerospace & Defense
etfs.summary: 0.58% expense ratio; broader diversification across commercial aerospace names (Boeing, GE Aerospace, RTX) continues to temper pure-play defense-tech volatility relative to ITA

etfs.name: Select STOXX Europe Defense
etfs.summary: ~$1.1B AUM across just 23 holdings, 0.5% expense ratio; BAE's climb to ~2,043p this week offset Rheinmetall's still-mixed sentiment, keeping the European sub-index's week roughly balanced

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: BAE Systems
positions.note: The ~11% recovery to ~2,043p this week reaffirms the record £84.0B H1 order backlog and raised full-year guidance (8-10% sales, 11-13% EPS growth) as the least-disputed thesis in the sector; weight raised on the price confirmation. Directly accessible from the UK with no wrapper needed — the most straightforward core holding on this page.

positions.name: AeroVironment
positions.note: The $464.8M Army LOCUST X3 laser award — the Pentagon's first-ever directed-energy production contract — diversifies AeroVironment's revenue beyond the drone segment and lands on top of a record $1.5B backlog; weight raised meaningfully, though the SCAR/BADGER securities-fraud litigation keeps this speculative rather than core. Also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: Kratos Defense
positions.note: Three sell-side targets and a Q2 beat-and-raise still support the CCA-engine optionality (GEK800 testing toward $150M of 2027 turbojet revenue), but Kratos again failed to place on the Sep 18 Gauntlet II leaderboard despite qualifying for both rounds — real evidence against the near-term autonomy-optionality case, so weight trimmed. Also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: L3Harris
positions.note: A new CEO and new board chair are now both in place and real contracts (the $4.7B Lockheed Martin deal, VAMPIRE/APKWS combat use in Ukraine) keep coming, but the Kubasik ouster still hasn't been explained and Golden Dome's FY27 funding is now understood to be zero — not just frozen — under a continuing resolution. Also sits in the Space sleeve via satellite work — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: Rheinmetall
positions.note: Shares recovered from ~€988 to ~€1,012-1,028 this week on a Marine Corps UGV order and Deutsche Bank's Buy call, but JPMorgan's Sep 10 Hold still sits awkwardly against 18-of-18 Buy ratings and a ~60% consensus upside gap; stays a watch until sentiment and price converge. Directly accessible from the UK without a US wrapper.

positions.name: Palantir
positions.note: UBS's third target hike this year (now $250) and a genuine AIPCon 11-driven demand story pushed shares to ~$177-178, but Karp's Sep 17 nationalization comments add a new regulatory-risk thread on top of Burry's unretracted sub-$100B case and a valuation still north of 100x trailing earnings. Also anchors the AI sleeve — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: Ondas Holdings
positions.note: Ascent Aerosystems missed the top five in Gauntlet II's Deep Strike category on top of the Q2 EPS miss and a Form 144 insider-sale filing — another data point reinforcing Avoid rather than a reason to reconsider it.

positions.name: Red Cat Holdings
positions.note: Teal Drones missed the top five in Gauntlet II's Close Quarters Battle category, the second straight negative data point after August's insider selling; moving this to Avoid until the maritime-autonomy and swarm-robotics story converts into contracted revenue rather than platform narrative.
